targets.summary: The sparsity_hint tests allocate real CUDA tensors, some of them large (1x32x2048x128). They should use fake tensors so they don't need real GPU allocation.
targets.adoption_evidence: Before: `q = torch.randn(1, 32, 2048, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)`, a real CUDA allocation. After the merge, that line sits inside `with FakeTensorMode():` and reads `q = torch.randn(1, 8, 64, 64, device="cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)`. The export calls that follow are inside the fake mode too. The `@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_CUDA, ...)` decorator was dropped. The test now checks flop counts instead of the roofline estimate, so it no longer needs real GPU tensors. This is what the maintainer asked for.
targets.stage3_reason: The test only inspects exported graph metadata, yet it allocates a real `torch.randn(1, 32, 2048, 128, device="cuda", ...)` and is gated with `@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_CUDA, ...)`, so it is skipped on CPU CI for no good reason. The merged code removed the CUDA skip and builds the inputs under `with FakeTensorMode():` on CPU, which is what the maintainer asked for.
